statement: Direct in-game evidence for exact Battlefield 6 attachment display strings. This is the ONLY route by which a name reaches GAME_VERIFIED_EXACT. Nothing here may be inferred, normalised, tidied or guessed: each record states what was actually read on screen, in which game version, and where the capture is kept. An empty observations list means no name is game-verified, which is the honest state until captures exist.

rules: gameVersion must equal the current live game version, otherwise the observation is recorded but NOT promoted: an exact name from an older patch is not evidence about the current one.
observedName is transcribed verbatim, including casing, spacing and punctuation. It is never cleaned up.
If observedName differs from the pinned source string, the observation wins for DISPLAY and the source string is preserved alongside it as a recorded discrepancy. Neither is deleted.

An attachment the classifier would otherwise treat as a generic tier or category label (every optic tier, bare barrel tiers) additionally requires acknowledgesTierAmbiguity: true. That flag is the recorder affirming they read the name of this specific catalogue entry, not the name of one member of a category the entry stands for. Without it, a category label could be silently converted into a fake product name.
reference must point at a retained capture (file path or durable URL). A description alone is not evidence.

exampleRecord.weaponContext: <weapon the attachment screen was opened from>
